title: Global airport website benchmark: calibrated expert-assessment matrix
status: Expert assessments with stated confidence. Not rankings, not usability-test results, not field performance data.

anchors.1: Absent or broken: the capability is missing or fails for most visitors.
anchors.2: Weak: present, but material defects block or mislead common tasks.
anchors.3: Adequate: the sector norm; core tasks possible with noticeable friction or gaps.
anchors.4: Strong: clearly above the sector norm, few material gaps, at least one distinctive feature.
anchors.5: Sector-leading: a reference implementation with no material gap on the website, verified first-hand.

calibration_rules: R1: a 5 requires first-hand observation; search-only or prior evidence caps a dimension at 4.5.
R2: confidence is at most medium for search-only evidence and low for prior-only evidence.
R3: the website is assessed; an app feature can support a score but cannot alone place the website above a peer whose equivalent web feature was observed.
R4: independent lab measurements made by this project (Lighthouse, axe-core, capture timings, page structure) are used as evidence where the original analyst did not have them.
R5: no score is raised without evidence recorded in the calibration log.

evidence_modes.direct: An analyst browsed the official site first-hand (captures, page reads, interaction scripts).
evidence_modes.partial-direct: Some official pages fetched first-hand before access was cut; the rest from search.
evidence_modes.search-plus-project-captures: Analyst report from web search; the project later captured screenshots and ran Lighthouse on the live site.
evidence_modes.search-only: No site content observed; web search and prior knowledge only.
evidence_modes.direct-structure-and-lab: MAHB: structure, HTML and lab audits observed first-hand; page content largely unreadable after the content API stopped serving the project network.

calibration_log.reason: The only 5 in the original set rested on search evidence alone, and the itinerary with gate walking time, security wait and alerts is an app feature. Per-flight web pages and bookable security slots are evidenced by search and justify the top of the observed range (4.5), not more.

iShopChangi, Changi Rewards and Changi Pay are well documented in official pages found by search, but no checkout was observed. Capped at 4.5, level with Heathrow (direct and search); confidence cannot be high on search alone.

Task efficiency was not observed (the report says 'not task-timed' and the homepage composition is prior knowledge). The highest observed UX score in the set is 4.0 (Heathrow, Haneda, Hong Kong, Istanbul, Incheon); an unobserved site should not sit above them.

The score rested on app-store ratings and app features; the report states 'Mobile web not observed'. Aligned with Heathrow (4.0), whose mobile web was rendered first-hand and whose app is similarly rated.

On the website only a searchable arrivals and departures listing is evidenced; saved flights, alerts, take-off-to-landing tracking and FlightSaver are app features. In both project captures the listing did not render and the page showed 'Unable to load' with a retry (cause not established). Every other 4.5 has an observed per-flight web page with journey assistance.

The score rested on the app rating; the report says the mobile web was not assessed. Project lab data: mobile homepage 21.0 MiB over 122 requests, Lighthouse performance 58 and accessibility 74. It cannot sit above Heathrow (4.0, 1.8 MiB, accessibility 92, similar app rating).

Project captures found no skip link, no main landmark and images without alt text on the homepage and departures page; Lighthouse accessibility 74 with button-name, link-name, label, image-alt and landmark-one-main failing. With the report's own negatives (indexed staging hosts, no accessibility statement, PDF sensory map) this matches Istanbul, Hamad and Munich (3.0), not Heathrow (3.5, skip link, accessibility 92).

The report's own evidence includes a mobile homepage of about 17 MB, 24 of 71 visible targets under 24 px and app alerts behind a member login; lab LCP 24.5 s. Heathrow (4.0) loads 1.8 MiB; Hong Kong and Istanbul, with comparable defects, hold 3.5.

Evidence is account-based rewards personalisation, app saved flights and a task chatbot dating from 2020; no generative or flight-aware assistant was found. Heathrow (4.0) has an evidenced AI agent on live data and Istanbul (4.0) login-free personalisation on the web. The analyst noted the AI search could not be run; confirmed current capability would restore 4.0.

Scored null in the report for lack of evidence. The project has since measured it: Lighthouse performance 58, LCP 7.9 s, TBT 379 ms, CLS 0.077, 21.0 MiB and 122 requests on the homepage; departures page about 0.9 MB in a capture. Comparable to Heathrow, Haneda and Istanbul (3.0). Low confidence: lab only, no header or incident evidence.

The board is the deepest in the set (nine fields, map deep links, codeshare grouping, timestamp, login-free bookmarks), but the report records no flight detail URL, no web alerts and no wait-time or walking-time context. Every other 4.5 adds a per-flight page with journey assistance; on board depth alone Hong Kong sits at 4.0, above Munich (3.5).

Previously prior knowledge only. Project screenshots show a restrained, image-led design with a unified flight and facility search in the hero and a consistent header; score confirmed, confidence raised.

Previously vendor claims only. Project screenshots show a coherent system (consistent type, palette and components), a task-first hero with flight search, quick tiles and a full Arabic build. Deduction kept for a modal cookie dialogue over the first view on desktop and mobile.

Project captures show flight search (airline, city or flight number) in the first view, working site search, and a contact launcher that puts feedback, lost and found, live chat, FAQs and contacts one tap away. Offsets from the report remain (bookings hand off to several partner platforms). Level with Hamad and Munich.

Project captures show a board with scheduled and actual times, terminal, gate, coloured status, a date selector and earlier flights, and a per-flight page with a 'Journey planner' timeline personalised by traveller type. Not higher: no update stamp was visible in the captured screens and no saved flights or web alerts are evidenced.

Score confirmed by project data: Lighthouse mobile performance 68 (the best valid run in the set), accessibility 100, CLS 0, 4.4 MiB; mobile board renders as cards. Held at 3.5 because the cookie dialogue covers the first mobile view and no official app is evidenced.

The report found no site search; a project capture shows one returning the accessibility services page first for 'wheelchair'. Lighthouse accessibility 100 (automated only). Offsets kept: English and Arabic only, no accessibility statement found, keyboard behaviour untested.

Project captures show a chat launcher on every captured page, 'Live chat support' in the contact launcher and a flight-page journey planner personalised by traveller type. With WhatsApp and a vendor-documented chatbot (search) this matches Hamad and Hong Kong (3.0). Chat not exercised, so confidence stays low.

Previously redirect timing only. Project lab: performance 68, TBT 26 ms, CLS 0, 4.4 MiB (the best valid Lighthouse result in the set); desktop load event about 2 s in a capture. Offsets kept: no HSTS on the redirect response and indexed development hosts (report).

MAHB's current passenger site scored for the first time on the same rubric from the consolidated audit and first-hand observations. See the MAHB section of the report for the evidence behind each score.

Checked against Hong Kong and Dubai (4.0 after calibration). Munich has a detail page, a login-free tracking strip and a freshness stamp, but no status styling, no alerts, no wait times and no journey timeline. 3.5 kept.
Rests on prior knowledge and the app; no page was seen. No evidence to move it either way; kept at 4.0 with low confidence and listed as a gap.

No speed data (the lab run measured a challenge page). Kept at 3.0 with low confidence as a neutral placeholder supported by search evidence on incident handling; Changi's null was replaced only because measurements exist.
Checked against Heathrow (4.0). Login-free WhatsApp updates and a needs-tailored journey directory are observed on the web; the chatbot was not. 4.0 kept.
Checked against Incheon (2.5). Similar Lighthouse performance (28 against 27) but Hong Kong's LCP is 8.9 s against 25.1 s and it sends transport security headers. 3.0 kept.

Detail pages, wait times and the connections planner are evidenced from page source and configuration rather than seen running. 4.5 kept at medium confidence; it is the only directly assessed 4.5 whose key features were not seen running.

caveats: Weighted totals are expert assessments by several analysts with different access, calibrated by one reviewer. Differences of up to about 3 percentage points are within the uncertainty of the method.

Lighthouse figures are lab measurements from one shared cloud container with mobile emulation and simulated slow 4G, with third-party hosts blocked; indicative only, not field data, not comparable with Chrome UX Report.
Automated accessibility checks (Lighthouse, axe-core) detect only part of WCAG; they are not conformance claims.
Schiphol was not measured: the Lighthouse result is a bot-challenge page.
